auth.notes: OAuth account flow for official enrollment/token APIs. The opaque AFI login token and broadcast key are separate per-lock credentials. No endpoint or real token is reproduced.

cloud.failure_mode: Fresh enrollment, new grants, renewal after expiry/revocation and vendor firmware lookup need the service. A locally cached unexpired AFI grant can still complete direct BLE without contacting it; passive state also works offline with the separate broadcast key. Current HA's failure to persist device keys is an implementation limitation, not a protocol requirement.
cloud.notes: A replacement cloud can cache/redistribute an existing grant but cannot mint lock-accepted tokens or complete signed enrollment without an authority the lock already trusts.
cloud.vendor_service: Danalock account/ekey service for enrollment and AFI-token issuance/renewal

companion_apps.name: Danalock
companion_apps.notes: Enrollment, credential issuance/renewal and vendor operation. A cached unexpired AFI token can later be used offline by a dedicated client.

companion_apps.name: Keaper
companion_apps.notes: Companion for locks already set up; not an independent offline enrollment route.

identity.notes: DMI serial is six bytes from the advertisement/device record. Do not infer or retain it from the BLE address and never publish a real serial in examples.

discovery.none: Manual exact-model selection required. Do not auto-activate lock control from company 0x01C8, the DMI UART service or an encrypted broadcast. Version-2 advertisements and the six-byte serial are validated only after the user selects a Danalock V3 and supplies the independent broadcast key.

manufacturer_data.description: DMI advertisements use Bluetooth company ID 456 (0x01C8, bytes C8 01 in the AD structure). Payload version 2 is normal DMI and version 3 is DFU. This is family evidence, not a safe automatic V3-lock matcher: Danapad and Universal Module share DMI. No executable company-ID matcher is declared; manually select the exact lock/radio variant.

identification.notes: The six-byte DMI serial in manufacturer payload bytes 1..6, not the possibly rotating BLE address, is the device identity. Redact it in shared captures.

device.manufacturer: Danalock / Salto Home Solution ApS (formerly Poly-Control)
device.name: Danalock V3 (DMI BLE)
device.notes:
Danalock V3's DMI BLE interface is a framed reliable stream carrying TLS 1.2 and AFI application messages. The GATT service is bce90001-c6eb-4ff8-bb6b-91cf6443c685, with writes to bce90002 and notifications from bce90003. Manufacturer company ID 0x01C8 identifies the broader DMI family, not a lock model by itself.
Consumer integration is identify_only: this project does not ship the dedicated frame/RPD/TLS/certificate/AFI session handler. There are no generic lock entities or plaintext commands. LockOperate is documented as advanced and attended only after a validated session and explicit owner confirmation; discovery or an automatic scan must never invoke it.
Two separate cloud-issued credentials have different jobs. The opaque AFI login token authorizes a TLS application session and has a validity window; the 16-byte broadcast key decrypts passive advertisements. One cannot substitute for the other. A cached, unexpired login token, lock serial and local DMI address can operate without a live cloud session. Passive state additionally needs the broadcast key. Initial enrollment, fresh token issuance, rotation and renewal still depend on the vendor signing service.

openness.notes: No official DMI wire specification was found. The pinned public Python implementation supersedes older static-only guesses about CRC reflection and mandatory client certificates.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Enrollment is an official cloud-signed flow, not an always-open local pairing window or a general PIN-pairing procedure.

procedures.basis: Vendor enrollment flow and public token/API documentation; not run by this project.
procedures.name: Official cloud-signed Danalock enrollment

steps.action: Use the official app/account to enroll the exact lock and obtain an owner-authorized AFI grant.
steps.expect: The lock accepts the issued grant during its validity interval; no independent CA authority is created.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the other central and start a fresh RPD/TLS session with a valid cached grant; do not use reset as a connection-troubleshooting shortcut.

pairing.notes: Security is application-layer DMI enrollment plus TLS server authentication and AFI token login. The TLS CertificateRequest does not imply mandatory client certificates: the compatible client returns an empty list and authenticates inside the encrypted AFI channel.

unpair.clears: Local user settings/enrollment; old grants are not assumed valid after the destructive ten-click reset.
unpair.notes: Targeted token revocation is cloud/permission management, not a demonstrated local self-keying/unpair operation.

safety_advisory.detail: Require manual model selection, full server-certificate validation, a cached unexpired token, successful AuthorityLogin and an attending person with an independent entry method. Send one intentional operation and wait for its result/state. A failed TLS session, expired token, timeout or absent result is not permission to retry actuation or disable validation.
safety_advisory.summary: AFI LockOperate physically moves a deadbolt. Never expose it to generic consumers, automatic discovery or unattended replay.

issued_to_client: Opaque AFI login token with valid_from/valid_to and permissions; required for control
Separate 16-byte AES broadcast key; required only for passive advertisement decode
Six-byte DMI lock serial and a local six-byte controller DMI address
Public DMI trust anchor, obtained out of band; public validation material, not a private key
credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi exists on the lock itself. Tokens are time/permission-limited bearer grants, not CA/exported ownership. The 12-hour refresh default in one integration is not a 12-hour TTL. No authoritative default/max TTL, predecessor invalidation or revocation-after-rotation rule is known. Never commit real login tokens, broadcast keys, serials or owner certs.
stored_on_device: Accepted AFI login grants and validity/permission state
Per-device broadcast key and lock/broadcast state

factory_reset.description: Salto's click-command guide assigns ten pinhole-button clicks to reset. This is destructive and not a way to obtain a new independent DMI token. Re-enrollment still needs the vendor signing service or a supported radio-specific controller.
factory_reset.effect: The official ten-click reset deletes all user settings. Treat DMI login grants, enrollment and client access as requiring re-provisioning; do not assume an old token survives. Radio-specific network/calibration effects must be checked before resetting a dual-radio lock.

procedures.basis: Official Salto Danalock click-command documentation and installation guide 226565; not executed here.
procedures.name: Ten clicks on the lock pinhole button

steps.action: Keep the door attended, preserve any required radio pairing material, and access the lock's pinhole button as shown by the official guide.
Activate the pinhole button ten times for factory reset.
steps.expect: User settings are deleted. Re-enroll through the official service or the chosen supported radio controller; old DMI credentials are not assumed valid.

cloud.local_alternative: No local initial enrollment is known. A cached unexpired AFI token works offline; Zigbee/Z-Wave/HomeKit radio-specific routes are noted separately and are not DMI self-enrollment.

methods.description: Use official enrollment or an owner-authorized token API export once, persist the token securely with its absolute validity interval, then use a dedicated local DMI client while it remains accepted. This does not export CA ownership or create permanent authority.
methods.name: Cloud-signed enrollment/export, then cached offline DMI

steps.action: Identify the exact V3 radio variant and preserve any existing Zigbee/Z-Wave/HomeKit pairing before changing app or hub enrollment.
Complete official cloud-signed enrollment or an owner-authorized AFI-token export; record serial, opaque login blob, valid_from/valid_to and permissions in a secret store.
steps.expect: A currently valid login grant exists. Do not log its bytes or confuse it with the broadcast key.

steps.action: For passive advertisements, separately store the 16-byte broadcast key; for every TLS session, configure the public DMI trust anchor and require full certificate validation.

Connect manually, subscribe to bce90003, establish frame/RPD/TLS, require an empty TLS client-certificate list followed by AFI AuthorityLogin status zero, then use read-only information/state/power requests first.
steps.expect: Read-only AFI responses succeed without cloud access. Stop on certificate, token, sequencing or dialect failure; no actuation follows automatically.

causes: This is expected, but the public-compatible client sends an empty certificate list. Authentication is the later AFI login token, not mandatory mutual-certificate TLS.
troubleshooting.symptom: The lock requests a client certificate during TLS.

causes: Persist the actual device login grant and validity, not only OAuth tokens. The current public HA integration does not persist device keys and requires cloud setup; that is not evidence cached DMI cannot work.
troubleshooting.symptom: A session works online but fails after restart offline.

causes: Do not connect. Check the exact DMI trust anchor, full chain/signature, serial/CN match and validity/constraints. Public certificate CN/serial alone is spoofable and is not authentication.
troubleshooting.symptom: Certificate validation succeeds only with insecure mode.

setup.notes: Normal enrollment is cloud-signed; there is no general local PIN pairing or unauthenticated self-keying path. A replacement client needs an owner-authorized export of a currently valid AFI login token, serial and local DMI address, plus the separate broadcast key for passive state and the public DMI trust anchor for certificate validation. Cached-token runtime is established by the public library and vendor cache design; token TTL/rotation behavior remains unknown.

rejoin.notes: A client with an accepted unexpired login token reconnects without cloud access. Expiry/revocation/rotation requires a fresh owner-authorized grant, not a reset workaround. Z-Wave/Zigbee network moves use their own exclude/include processes; HomeKit needs its preserved pairing code.

steps.action: Check the token's absolute validity and the exact serial/variant before reconnecting; close any other central.
Establish a newly sequenced RPD/TLS session with full certificate validation and repeat AuthorityLogin plus read-only checks.

testing.notes: No Danalock hardware, account, owner token, broadcast key or certificate operation was used by this project. Frame/RPD/broadcast fixtures below are synthetic. The public implementation author reports live verification on BTZE only; BT, BTZB/BTZBE and dual-mode BTHK DMI compatibility are extrapolations, not independently verified. Public implementation tests and firmware analysis do not change this spec's untested status.

variants.notes: Plain Bluetooth variant. Cached-token DMI is the only documented local route; community live compatibility is not independently verified.
Z-Wave + BLE. BTZE is EU and the only variant on which the community author reports DMI live verification; BTZU is US. Z-Wave JS is a separate local survival route.
Zigbee + BLE. Zigbee2MQTT supports V3-BTZB/V3-BTZBE independently of the vendor cloud. DMI BLE compatibility is unverified here.
HomeKit variant; preserve HomeKit pairing material and use local HomeKit. Dual-mode firmware 2.7.5 additionally enables account-based DMI, but community DMI compatibility is unverified.

evidence.app_and_firmware_analysis: The two vendor apps and native protocol library established GATT/company IDs, enrollment and credential roles. Public firmware packages established Nordic DFU metadata and the shared DMI trust-anchor fingerprint. No owner blob, CA private key, token or certificate signing was used.

local_access.summary: Direct DMI BLE with cached credentials and a dedicated secure session handler. identify_only in this catalogue because that handler and full X.509 validation are not shipped.

device_get_information.response: Seven varints: product, hardware major/minor/revision, firmware major/minor/revision; then NUL-terminated UTF-8 firmware identifier

lock_get_settings.response: TLV settings; member 4 is unsupported and must not be written

lock_operate.advanced_reason: Moves a real lock. Only after manual selection, full certificate validation, valid login and an attending person; send once and require result/state, never auto-replay.

power_source_get_information.response: TLV members: 1 power type, 2 level, 3 battery percent, 4 uint16; validate actual members before exposing units

messages.result: 02 | class u8 | function u8 | status u8 | payload; match strictly in request order (no request id)

primitives.strings: Varint byte length followed by bytes
primitives.tlv: Varint tag, varint length, value; unsigned integers inside values are shortest big-endian (zero is one 00 byte)
primitives.varint: Unsigned LEB128, 7 data bits per byte, high bit continuation; reject truncation and negative input

session: After RPD+TLS, send AuthorityLogin class 1 function 1 with the opaque login token appended directly; require result status 0 before any other feature.
Set UTC with class 3 function 1 payload uint32 LE epoch seconds, then perform read-only information/state/power requests. Requests are sequential, one pending at a time.
Pre-check valid_from/valid_to locally but still require the lock's acceptance. Expiry, token status 0x5E..0x73 or not-logged-in 0x41 requires a fresh grant, not insecure/replay fallback.

plaintext.authentication_note: CBC has no authentication tag; the inner CRC catches corruption/wrong keys but is not a cryptographic authenticity boundary.

consumer_limitations.required_handler: Manual variant selection + DMI frame/RPD + TLS 1.2 + full certificate validation + AFI token login + advanced attended actuation gate.

escaping.decode: The public codec accepts C2 B as B|0x80 and preserves a trailing lone C2 for resync tolerance; canonical writers emit only the three pairs above.
escaping.encode: C0 -> C2 40; C1 -> C2 41; C2 -> C2 42. No other byte is escaped.

logical_layout.name: destination

logical_layout.description: High nibble receiver port, low nibble sender port; lock port 2, client chooses random 4-bit port
logical_layout.name: ports

logical_layout.description: Low nibble sender sequence, high nibble next expected peer sequence; both modulo 16
logical_layout.name: seq_ack

dmi_frame.provenance: Public synthetic pydanalock-ble fixtures. Addresses and payload are invented; no captured traffic or owner identifiers.
dmi_frame.validation: Minimum logical length 19 and magic 00 F1; validate CRC before delivery. Stream decoder discards noise before C0, buffers incomplete trailing frames, emits glued frames in order and drops malformed/bad-CRC frames.

radio_survival_notes.bthk: Use Apple Home or Home Assistant HomeKit Device locally and preserve the pairing code. Single-controller pairing and RF quality matter. Dual-mode firmware 2.7.5 adds account-based DMI but does not prove community DMI compatibility.
radio_survival_notes.btzb_btzbe: Zigbee2MQTT supports V3-BTZB/V3-BTZBE with lock/state, battery, PIN users, action events and OTA. BTZB is pre-2020 Zigbee 1.2 and cannot be Zigbee-updated; BTZBE is Zigbee 3.0/updateable. No Danabridge/cloud is needed for that Zigbee path.
radio_survival_notes.btze_btzu: Z-Wave JS supports Danalock V3-BTZE with manufacturer 0x010E, product type/id 0x0009/0x0001. Enroll in the app first if BLE is also wanted; hub-first disables BLE. BTZE is EU, BTZU US.
radio_survival_notes.danabridge: Only needed for out-of-range vendor-cloud relay, not for direct in-range BLE. No local replacement for its cloud router is established.
radio_survival_notes.danapad: App-less Danapad pairing is not general DMI self-keying: it deletes existing PIN codes and prevents later addition to the Danalock app. It can preserve PIN operation with a supported hub.
radio_survival_notes.scope: Alternative local routes for owners, not extra specs or evidence that DMI works on every variant.

rules: SYN consumes the sender sequence immediately. Peer SYN carries its own initial sequence and ack=initiator ISN+1.
Sending data does not advance the sender sequence. Only a data-path frame (data or empty ACK, type 0) whose ack equals current own sequence+1 advances it.
Empty ACK frames never consume a sequence number. SYN/FIN ack nibbles are handshake bookkeeping and never advance data acknowledgement state.
Deliver non-empty data only when seq equals receiver expected; then increment expected. Drop duplicate/out-of-order data silently without re-acknowledgement.
An in-order FIN consumes the receiver sequence, so the response ack is fin_seq+1. FIN does not consume the sender's own sequence at construction.
Window one: retain and retransmit the identical unacknowledged frame up to 3 retries 2000 ms apart. SYN-ACK window 4500 ms; post-FIN teardown window 6000 ms.
rpd.sequence: Four-bit modulo-16 counters with random initial sequence numbers. Low seq_ack nibble is sender sequence; high nibble is next expected peer.

negative_cases: Repeating lock data seq=1 is a duplicate: phone_peer_next stays 2 and no new ACK is generated.
Lock data seq=3 while expecting 2 is out of order: drop silently.
An empty ACK with ack unequal to own_seq+1 does not advance own_seq.
An in-order FIN at peer seq=2 changes phone_peer_next to 3; its final ACK carries high nibble 3.

certificate_validation.insecure_mode: forbidden; never disable certificate-chain or serial-equivalent identity checks
certificate_validation.public_client_warning: The reviewed HA integration disables verification and the library's optional secure mode misses validity/constraints; neither behavior meets this spec's required profile.
required_checks: Require the exact trusted DMI anchor by fingerprint and verify every certificate signature/chain cryptographically; CN or serial alone is not authentication.
Require the leaf subject CN and X.509 serial to match the connected six-byte lock serial and validate the leaf ECDSA P-256 key/proof.
Check leaf and anchor validity intervals, Basic Constraints (anchor is a CA), and key usage. Reject expired/not-yet-valid leaves and non-CA anchors.
Handle the public anchor's year-zero-to-9999 validity with a DMI-aware X.509 parser rather than weakening checks because a general-purpose library cannot represent year zero.
Document the absence of an established revocation mechanism instead of silently treating it as successful revocation checking. CT/public-web roots are separate and do not replace the DMI anchor.
certificate_validation.trust_anchor: Caller-supplied public DMI intermediate; this is not a public-web-CA hostname validation problem

empty_client_certificate.requirement: The lock sends CertificateRequest; client returns an empty Certificate message, then authenticates with AFI AuthorityLogin. No TLS client private key/certificate is required.

tls_12.extended_master_secret: SHA-384 over handshake messages ClientHello through ClientKeyExchange inclusive, including each handshake header. Wrong transcript boundaries cause Finished failure.
tls_12.extensions: Extended master secret required; signature algorithms ecdsa/sha512/sha384/sha256; uncompressed EC point; encrypt-then-mac offered
tls_12.groups: Offer X25519 and secp256r1 plus the public profile's other groups; require secp256r1 selection

prf_sha384_test_vector.provenance: Synthetic RFC 5246 PRF vector from the public implementation; no session secret.

tls_12.profile: TLS 1.2 over the reliable byte stream; phone is client, lock is server

additional_authenticated_data.length_semantics: The last two bytes are the PLAINTEXT length, excluding the 8-byte explicit nonce and 16-byte GCM tag. This is not the 5-byte TLS record header and not the encrypted body length.

records.client_finished: Handshake type 0x16 record, explicit nonce 0, plaintext 14 00 00 0c plus 12-byte verify_data
records.lock_finished: Accept the lock Finished in an application-data 0x17 record with nonce 0; do not require record type 0x16
records.malformed: Reject unexpected cipher/group, missing EMS, invalid ECDSA proof, wrong certificate, bad GCM tag or unexpected handshake order. Never authenticate with the bare 5-byte record header or with the encrypted body length in AAD.
records.protection: AES-256-GCM; 8-byte explicit nonce equal to the per-direction record counter starting at 1 for application data. The 96-bit nonce is the direction's 4-byte fixed IV followed by those 8 explicit bytes.

tls_12.server_key_exchange: P-256 uncompressed 65-byte point; ECDSA SHA-512 signature over ClientHello.random || ServerHello.random || params, verified against the certified server key

remaining_unknowns: Default/custom token TTL, maximum lifetime, predecessor invalidation/revocation and long-term cached-token acceptance.
DMI compatibility on BT, BTZB/BTZBE and dual-mode BTHK; only BTZE has author-reported live evidence.
Full offline enrollment/self-keying and any authority accepted for owner-independent token issuance.
Production certificate revocation behavior and a maintained reference implementation with complete X.509 checks.
Exact battery_raw scaling and all Power Source TLV member semantics across variants.
Bootloader signature enforcement, anti-downgrade policy, interrupted-update recovery and Danabridge trust enforcement.

characteristics.notes: C0..C1 escaped DMI frames split into <=20-byte chunks. Only a dedicated validated session handler may write.

characteristics.notes: Arbitrary stream fragments; reassemble before frame CRC and RPD processing. CCCD is the standard 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.

services.name: DMI BLE UART service
services.notes: Custom framed reliable byte stream carrying TLS and AFI. Not an identity signal and not a plaintext UART. No characteristic commands are declared for generic consumers.
